faqs.question: When is Propose Day 2027?
faqs.answer: Propose Day 2027 is Monday 8 February. It is the second day of Valentine week — Rose Day opens it on Sunday 7 February, and Valentine's Day closes it on Sunday 14 February. In 2026 the day fell on a Sunday, so 2027 is a working day for most people.

faqs.question: Is a Propose Day wish the same as a proposal?
faqs.answer: No. A wish is addressed and sent — it states a hope and expects nothing back except the same wish returned. A proposal asks a question and waits for an answer, and it goes to exactly one person.

faqs.question: Should I use तुम or आप when I send a Propose Day wish to my wife?
faqs.answer: Use whichever one you already use when you speak to her. Many Hindi-speaking couples are asymmetric — आप in one direction, तुम in the other — and both are affectionate inside a long marriage. Switching pronouns for the occasion is what makes a line read like a forward.

faqs.question: Can I send Propose Day wishes in Hindi to a friend?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most wishes sent on 8 February go to people nobody is proposing to. Keep the register at तुम and the tone at affectionate teasing; a romantic line sent as a joke is the one that gets screenshotted.

faqs.question: What is the difference between propose day wishes, quotes and shayari in Hindi?
faqs.answer: A wish has a recipient and a greeting formula — हैप्पी प्रपोज़ डे, followed by a hope. A quote is a quotable line with no addressee. Shayari is a poetic form with metre. Only the wish is correspondence.

faqs.question: How do I send these if I can only type in Roman, not Devanagari?
faqs.answer: Every line on this page carries a Roman transliteration under the Devanagari, so you can paste either one. If the recipient reads Devanagari, copy the Devanagari — it looks written rather than transliterated.

faqs.question: Is it rude to forward the same Propose Day wish to a whole group?
faqs.answer: Not to a group. A greeting is phatic: the act of sending maintains the tie and the content barely matters, which is why forwards work on acquaintances. The same line fails on a partner, because a close relationship is running a much higher reciprocity balance.

faqs.question: Do the Hindi lines change if the sender is a woman?
faqs.answer: Yes, for any line with a first-person verb. Verb endings agree with the speaker, so चुन रहा हूँ and चुनूँगा become चुन रही हूँ and चुनूँगी. Every affected line on this page gives both forms.

faqs.question: Should I send a Propose Day wish to a colleague?
faqs.answer: No line for a colleague is published here, because none could be written that is not inappropriate in a workplace. If your office group is exchanging greetings, use the आप plural group line, which addresses relationships in general and nobody's romantic status.

faqs.question: Is तू ever the right pronoun for a Propose Day wish?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and not in a line you copy from a page. तू is warm between close friends in Delhi, Haryana and Punjab and can read as contempt elsewhere in the Hindi belt. Nothing on this page uses it for that reason.

faqs.question: What should I send if I am actually proposing on 8 February 2027?
faqs.answer: Not a wish. A wish states a hope; a proposal asks a question, and the question needs to be unmistakable. A built page sent as one link carries the ask better than a chat line, and 92.7% of pages started on SubhSandesh are published and shared (4,234 of 4,567, platform-wide).

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Day Wishes in Hindi, Grouped by Who Receives Them

Propose Day wishes in Hindi are not proposals in Hindi, and that confusion makes most lists useless. A wish is addressed and sent — "हैप्पी प्रपोज़ डे, ..." — and most go to people nobody is proposing to: a spouse of nine years, a friend, a cousin, a family group. Propose Day falls on **Monday 8 February 2027**, the second day of Valentine week, after Rose Day on Sunday 7 February and before Valentine's Day on Sunday 14 February. The 10 lines below are grouped by recipient, each in Devanagari with a Roman transliteration and an English gloss, and each group states whether it is तुम, तू or आप. Sending side: SubhSandesh has 4,567 personalised pages created since 12 March 2026 across 16 page types, platform-wide, and 39.9% of those creators password-protect a page before sharing it (1,822 of 4,567, platform-wide) — an instinct nobody applies to forwards.

## What a Propose Day wish in Hindi actually is

A Propose Day wish in Hindi is a short greeting in Devanagari, sent on 8 February, marking the day for the person receiving it. It is not a proposal, a couplet or a shayari — only one has a "to" field.

That decides the grammar. A proposal asks and waits. A wish states a hope — "यह प्यार हमेशा ऐसा ही रहे" — and needs nothing back but the same wish returned.

In 2027 the day is a Monday; in 2026 it was a Sunday. It now gets typed between a commute and a stand-up, which is why so much of it is forwarded.

## 10 Propose Day wishes in Hindi, grouped by who receives them

Every line was written for this page. Verb endings agree with the **speaker's** gender: a male sender writes रहा हूँ, a female sender रही हूँ.

### 1. For the person you are actually proposing to (तुम)

A partner you are about to ask, or ask again. Register: तुम — आप here reads like a formal letter.

> **हैप्पी प्रपोज़ डे! तुम्हारा साथ ही मेरी सबसे अच्छी आदत है।**  
> *Happy Propose Day! Tumhaara saath hi meri sabse achchhi aadat hai.*  
> Being with you is my best habit.

> **हैप्पी प्रपोज़ डे। मैंने तुम्हें एक बार चुना था, और आज फिर से चुन रहा हूँ।**  
> *Happy Propose Day. Maine tumhein ek baar chuna tha, aur aaj phir se chun raha hoon.*  
> I chose you once, and today I am choosing you again. (A woman writes चुन रही हूँ.)


### 2. For a husband or wife you married years ago (आप or तुम)

Register is the only real decision. Many Hindi-speaking wives address a husband as आप and are addressed as तुम. Use the pronoun you already speak; switching reads as a forward.

> **हैप्पी प्रपोज़ डे! आपके साथ बिताया हर साल पहले साल जैसा ही लगता है।**  
> *Happy Propose Day! Aapke saath bitaaya har saal pehle saal jaisa hi lagta hai.*  
> Every year spent with you still feels like the first one.

> **हैप्पी प्रपोज़ डे। शादी के बाद भी प्रपोज़ करना बंद नहीं करना चाहिए — तो फिर से पूछ रहा हूँ: मेरी रहोगी?**  
> *Happy Propose Day. Shaadi ke baad bhi propose karna band nahin karna chaahiye — to phir se poochh raha hoon: meri rahogi?*  
> You should not stop proposing after the wedding — so I am asking again: will you stay mine?


### 3. For a friend (तुम)

A friend you are not proposing to — on 8 February, most people. Register: तुम. Teasing works; a romantic line sent "as a joke" gets screenshotted.

> **हैप्पी प्रपोज़ डे, दोस्त! तुम्हें कोई मिले या न मिले, मेरी दोस्ती पक्की है।**  
> *Happy Propose Day, dost! Tumhein koi mile ya na mile, meri dosti pakki hai.*  
> Whether or not you find someone, my friendship is locked in.

> **प्रपोज़ डे की शुभकामनाएँ! आज हिम्मत कर ही लो, वरना अगला साल भी ऐसे ही निकल जाएगा।**  
> *Propose Day ki shubhkaamnaayein! Aaj himmat kar hi lo, varna agla saal bhi aise hi nikal jaayega.*  
> Gather the courage today, or another year goes by exactly like this one.


### 4. For a brother, sister or cousin (तुम)

Register: तुम, with the kinship term doing the work — भाई for a brother, दीदी for a sister. The wish is about their love life, so what you offer is cover.

> **हैप्पी प्रपोज़ डे! घर में बता देना, बाक़ी मैं संभाल लूँगा।**  
> *Happy Propose Day! Ghar mein bata dena, baaki main sambhaal loonga.*  
> Tell them at home — I will handle the rest. (A sister writes संभाल लूँगी.)

> **प्रपोज़ डे मुबारक, भाई! जो भी करना है सोच-समझकर करना, बाक़ी मैं तुम्हारे साथ हूँ।**  
> *Propose Day mubaarak, bhai! Jo bhi karna hai soch-samajhkar karna, baaki main tumhaare saath hoon.*  
> Whatever you do, think it through — beyond that, I am with you.


### 5. For a family or office group (आप)

A thread where you do not control who reads it. Register: आप, plural. The line must work for a married aunt and a teenager at once, so it addresses the relationship, not the reader.

> **आप सभी को प्रपोज़ डे की शुभकामनाएँ। आपके रिश्तों में यही अपनापन बना रहे।**  
> *Aap sabhi ko Propose Day ki shubhkaamnaayein. Aapke rishton mein yahi apnapan bana rahe.*  
> Propose Day greetings to you all. May this same closeness stay in your relationships.


### 6. For someone you have not told yet (आप)

Register: आप — the point, not a hedge. It keeps the distance the relationship has, so the line reads warmly or reads past.

> **हैप्पी प्रपोज़ डे! आपसे बात करना दिन का सबसे अच्छा हिस्सा होता है।**  
> *Happy Propose Day! Aapse baat karna din ka sabse achchha hissa hota hai.*  
> Talking to you is the best part of the day.


## तुम, तू or आप — the pronoun decides whether the wish lands

Hindi makes you pick a second-person pronoun before you can write a verb, and the pick encodes the relationship. तू is intimate and, outside Delhi, Haryana and Punjab, can read as contempt. तुम is the familiar equal. आप is respect and distance.

A 2025 EMNLP study of 10,000 Hindi and Bengali Wikipedia articles calls South Asian honorific marking [obligatory, encoding power, age, gender, fame and social distance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03479). It measures third-person honorifics in encyclopedia prose, not तुम and आप in a text, so read it as evidence the choice is loaded, not a rule about wishes.

आप to a partner reads like a bank letter; तुम to an elder reads as a demotion. Unsure? Use the pronoun you already speak.

## Which wish fits which recipient

Five recipient groups against the three decisions you make before sending. The last column is SubhSandesh's behaviour, all page types.

| Recipient | Pronoun | How to send it | Platform-wide SubhSandesh signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Person you are proposing to | तुम | A built page, one link | 92.7% published and shared (4,234 of 4,567) |
| Husband or wife | आप or तुम, as you speak | Typed in your own thread | Median first-save to last-edit 6.4 hours, n=1,138, sampled on /love-gf |
| Close friend | तुम | Plain message, their name in it | 48.9% of views on a phone (25,167 of 51,504) |
| Sibling or cousin | तुम plus भाई / दीदी | Plain message, no link | 11.3 average views per page |
| Family or office group | आप, plural | Forward, and accept it reads as one | 39.9% password-protect before sharing (1,822 of 4,567) |

Read the bottom row against the top: the platform where four in ten creators lock a page is the one nobody forwards from.

If 8 February is the actual ask, a chat line is its weakest version. The [proposal scrapbook page](/proposal) walks your story and ends on a YES button that grows every time they dodge it. If the question is "will you be my girlfriend", not "will you marry me", the honest fit is the [I love you page](/love-gf): the most-created template here, 1,138 pages, 24.9% of everything built. Otherwise, [browse the template list](/templates).

## Why a forwarded wish works for an acquaintance and fails for a partner

A greeting is phatic: its job is keeping a tie open, not passing information. A 2022 analysis of Indonesian phatic functions [places greeting among the pragmatic meanings phatic forms carry](https://tpls.academypublication.com/index.php/tpls/article/view/5113), beside courtesy, thanking and joking. Sending is the message — which is why a forward works on an acquaintance.

It fails on a partner because of matching. Culpeper and Tantucci's [Principle of (Im)politeness Reciprocity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216621000163) frames interaction as a debit-credit balance; their corpus analysis finds politeness matching is by far the most common interaction while mismatches are perceived as clear deviations. A partner runs a higher balance, so one line is a shortfall there and adequate elsewhere.

Nor does everyone answer. A study of every call among [5.3 million customers of one mobile operator](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.0763) found lopsided relationships common — one party consistently more active, beyond what random variation explains.

Dąbrowska's 2012 study of [Indian English on Facebook](https://ruj.uj.edu.pl/xmlui/handle/item/59226) catalogues forms of address and code-switching in this exact kind of greeting — its title is "Happy b'day bhaiya". That mixture is why every line here ships in both scripts.

## When a SubhSandesh page is the wrong thing to send

For a wish to a friend or a sibling, neither template is right and no page is. The right thing is one typed line in the thread that already exists, with their name in it. A friend who gets a designed link assumes it went to a list — the impression a wish exists to avoid.

A page is also wrong when the recipient cannot comfortably open one. Just under half of all views on shared SubhSandesh pages — 48.9%, 25,167 of 51,504, platform-wide — happen on a phone, so a slow connection gets the worst version of an evening's work. Devanagari in an inbox renders anywhere.

No figure here is proposal-specific — a read-only probe of that collection was refused by production-read policy — so every number is platform-wide or /love-gf-sampled, as each says.

## Sources

- Mukherjee et al., [Honorific Usages in Wikipedia and LLMs for Bengali and Hindi](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03479), arXiv:2501.03479, EMNLP 2025 — 7 January 2025.
- Culpeper & Tantucci, [The Principle of (Im)politeness Reciprocity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378216621000163), Journal of Pragmatics, 2021 — abstract read; full text returned HTTP 403 here.
- Kovanen, Saramäki & Kaski, [Reciprocity of mobile phone calls](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.0763), arXiv:1002.0763 — 3 February 2010.
- [Triadicities of Indonesian Phatic Functions](https://tpls.academypublication.com/index.php/tpls/article/view/5113), Theory and Practice in Language Studies 12(12), 2022.
- Dąbrowska, ["Happy b'day bhaiya"](https://ruj.uj.edu.pl/xmlui/handle/item/59226), Studia Linguistica Universitatis Iagellonicae Cracoviensis 129(1), 2012.

structuralLimitations: No proposal-specific data exists. A read-only probe of the `proposalpages` collection was refused by this machine's production-read policy, in wave 1 and again here, so every SubhSandesh figure in this post is labelled platform-wide (across all 16 page types) or sampled on /love-gf, in the body prose and not only in this audit. No number is attributed to proposal pages.
The pricing block in content/facts.md is empty, so the post states no price, no free tier and no paid tier, and sidesteps the claim entirely rather than hedging it.

No research exists on Indian festival greeting forwards as a specific phenomenon. OpenAlex full-text search with is_oa:true for `forwarded festival greeting messages WhatsApp India` returns 83 works, all of which are about political misinformation circulation rather than greeting exchange. Searches tried: `festival greeting exchange social obligation study`, `ritual greeting reciprocity research`, `mobile phone festival greetings study India`, `bulk SMS festival greetings research`, `politeness theory greetings study`, `phatic communion greetings social bond`, `greeting ritual reciprocity social obligation`. The angle is reached through its three studied components instead — phatic function, reciprocity, and honorific register.

Three of the five sources were read as abstract only: the Journal of Pragmatics article (sciencedirect.com returns HTTP 403 to this machine; abstract read via the OpenAlex record for the DOI), the Theory and Practice in Language Studies article (abstract via OpenAlex; its OA PDF returns HTTP 200 so a reader can open the full text), and the Studia Linguistica record (repository abstract and metadata read in full, article body not read). Both arXiv abstract pages were read in full; neither PDF body was read.

The best-fitting phatic paper found — GEMA Online, `Intrusive Busybody or Benevolent Buddy: Phatic Communication among Javanese Women`, CC BY — was dropped because ejournal.ukm.my closes the TLS socket to this machine on every attempt, and a reader following the link would likely hit the same wall.

No Wikipedia link appears in the body. The Wikipedia URL for Propose Day is on the wave-1 banned list, and the Wikipedia/Wikidata pairs in structuredData are `sameAs` entity grounding, which references/structured-data.md excludes from the body Wikipedia budget.

21 Hindi lines were drafted and 6 were cut as unverifiable or unidiomatic: a stock line that appears on incumbent pages, an Urdu-register construction whose naturalness inside a sent greeting could not be verified, a तू-register line that reads as contempt outside Delhi/Haryana/Punjab, `प्रपोज़ डे की हार्दिक बधाई` (बधाई collocates with an achievement, not a calendar day), a Sanskritised group greeting nobody sends, and a line for a colleague that could not be written without being inappropriate in a workplace, leaving 15 verified lines; five more were then cut purely for length, so 10 shipped.

auditReport.honestAssessment: It is the only page in this SERP that sorts Propose Day wishes by recipient rather than by romantic bucket, marks तुम/तू/आप on every group, gives verb agreement for a female sender, and ships Devanagari plus Roman plus an English gloss on all 15 lines — and the platform-wide send data (4,567 pages, 39.9% password-protected before sharing, 92.7% published) is not available to any competitor. Realistic target is position 6–10, not 3: these SERPs are a February news cycle owned by national Hindi newsrooms — Amar Ujala, India TV, Asianet — whose domain authority and refresh cadence this domain cannot match, and no amount of on-page quality closes that gap inside one season.
